traces.name: merge_intervals
traces.title: Write merge_intervals against a visible test suite
traces.note: The programming setting. Every node is a complete program and the reward is the fraction of tests it passes, so simulation is skipped. The one-pass approach looks best to the model and caps at three of five; the fix is a different branch, not a better patch.

traces.name: game_of_24
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: All six operations, including simulation: the tree descends greedily by value, in the real environment, until one number is left. Solved on the fifth iteration, after four dead ends.

traces.name: game_of_24_no_value
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: Ablation: lambda = 0, so V(s) is self-consistency alone and the model's own judgement is thrown away. It still gets there, but it needs every iteration it has and half again as many nodes.

traces.name: game_of_24_greedy
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: Ablation: w = 0, so UCT collapses to pure exploitation and selection never leaves the branch it liked first. It grows a larger tree than the full search and never finds 24 at all.

traces.name: multihop_qa
traces.title: Two-hop question answering with a retrieval tool
traces.note: Two-hop retrieval. The corpus holds a tempting near-miss answer, and the policy has a recency bias that walks straight into it; the second iteration backs out and finds the right document.

traces.name: multihop_qa_no_reflection
traces.title: Two-hop question answering with a retrieval tool
traces.note: Ablation: reflection off. Identical outcome, one step shorter - which is the paper's own finding. Reflection is the smallest of its three ablations; the value function and the search structure matter more.
